title: Require execution authorization regardless of Skill manifest claims
goal: Ensure every Skill executor invocation requires an explicit execute capability grant even when an installed manifest declares only read or another weaker capability set.
context: Issue #347 requires runtime-owned authorization rather than trusting capability claims in imported Skill manifests. SkillRuntime currently evaluates only manifest.requiredCapabilities before invoking an explicitly registered executor, so a manifest declaring [.read] can be executed by a read-only policy.
forbidden_changes: Do not trust manifest-declared capabilities as grants or bypass policy, approval, schema, cancellation, or output verification.
Do not add arbitrary executor mappings or broaden workspace capability exposure.
Do not modify UI, provider/GGUF, or unrelated runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: SkillRuntime always includes execute in the policy intent before invoking any Skill executor.
A Skill manifest declaring only read cannot execute through a policy that grants read but denies execute.
Existing registered executor, fail-closed, approval, cancellation, and verification tests remain passing.
M3, Agent Task Contract, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm M3, Agent Task Contract, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA checks on the final PR head.
recovery: If the regression test exposes an unexpected policy contract, preserve fail-closed execution and adapt only the authorization boundary and focused test; do not weaken the test or claim verification before required checks pass.
